title: #86 Neeraj Khemlani & Matt Ankrum: The Coffee Can Investor

reader_summary.headline: Matt Ankrum explains his coffee can investing strategy and shares lessons from history.
reader_summary.overview: Matt Ankrum describes a strategy of holding a small number of stocks for decades. He focuses on exceptional companies with strong advantages and avoids emotional selling. The episode also discusses how parents can teach children about money and long-term thinking.

key_points.text: A coffee can portfolio holds 10 to 20 stocks for 30 years to capture massive long-term gains.
key_points.evidence_quote: how I actually described that coffee can is one in that I look at it and say it's over a 30-year time frame.

key_points.text: Parents teach kids to ask why a business matters before investing, helping them understand value.
key_points.evidence_quote: And they'll ask, well, what do they do? Why does that matter? Why would the customer care about that? And then why couldn't somebody else do that same thing?

key_points.text: Investors must study history and market cycles to understand how innovations transform industries over time.
key_points.evidence_quote: I'm a big believer for anybody who wants to be long-term investing or who is just serious investor, is that you have to be a student of history. You have to be a student of the markets and understanding cycles and other things that go on.

reader_summary.why_it_matters: Listeners learn to hold great companies tightly through short-term volatility and avoid common emotional mistakes.
